summary.headline: India Glycols Q1 FY27 net revenue rose 9% to INR1,130 crore and record EBITDA of INR170 crore (+13%), with PAT up 32%.
summary.overview: Consolidated net revenue reached INR1,130 crore (+9% YoY) and EBITDA INR170 crore (+13%), with EBITDA margin at 15.0% versus 14.3%. Management said PAT rose 32% and finance costs fell to INR25 crore from INR45 crore on debt reduction. The NCLT sanctioned the demerger scheme on 17 July 2026 and the company is now reporting under three entities. Management attributed part of the quarter's gains to the war-driven crude spike, which made bio-based EO competitive with Reliance's product again. Sequential EBITDA comparison is distorted by Q4 FY26 including about INR39 crore of Clariant dividend income.

segments.name: IGL Spirits (potable spirits)
segments.commentary: Spirits net revenue INR371 crore with EBITDA margin 22.9% (+207 bps). IMFL revenue grew 26% to 1.4 million cases (+55% volume); non-IMFL revenue was flat at INR279 crore with volume of 7.5 million cases (+6%).

segments.name: Bio-Fuel (ethanol)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR323 crore (+7%), EBIT INR27 crore (+19%), EBIT margin 8.4%; management also cited EBITDA margin of 10.8% (+250 bps).

segments.name: Chemicals (India Glycols)
segments.commentary: Chemicals revenue INR332 crore (+25%) at 11.4% EBITDA margin; small gases INR13 crore at 23.1% margin. Glycols value up 83%; green solvents and glycol ethers volume +6%, value +13%, gross margin close to 50%. Performance chemicals grew 40%, below target.

segments.name: Ennature Bio Pharma
segments.commentary: Best-ever quarter at INR83 crore revenue (per call) / INR90 crore net revenue under new structure, up 53-65%; EBITDA up ~188% per the prepared remarks. Nicotine sales doubled QoQ on European customer conversions; thiocolchicoside up 26% QoQ.

segments.name: Clariant JV (Kashipur)
segments.commentary: JV net revenue up 21% QoQ with EBITDA up in high double digits QoQ; JV profit cited at about INR21 crore versus about INR19 crore a year earlier.

guidance_outlook: IGL Spirits: EBITDA above INR500 crore for FY27 (INR120 crore already delivered in Q1); IMFL volume to roughly double versus FY26 (FY26 IMFL volume 3.4 million cases).
Spirits: management expects healthy double-digit growth in FY28 and aims to be debt-free from FY28; target EBITDA above INR1,000 crore in four to five years.

Chemicals aspiration (explicitly not a projection): EBITDA about INR400 crore and revenue about INR2,500 crore in four to five years; FY27 revenue aspiration INR150 crore-plus for the new performance chemicals business; margin targeted to rise toward 30% gross margin.
Ennature aspiration: EBITDA INR130-150 crore over the next four to five years.
Capex in chemicals expected to be small: INR5-20 crore incremental in the current year; no INR400-500 crore plant expected for at least two years.
capex_capacity: Chemicals capex plans: incremental INR5-10 crore, possibly up to INR15-20 crore this year, via modular expansion; new plant additions to date about INR50-60 crore.
Ennature started nicotine crude processing at its Kashipur plant, adding capacity.
Spirits: captive ENA capacity described as sufficient, supporting cost advantage in UP, Uttarakhand and Delhi.

Demerger: after effectiveness, Spirits, Bio-Fuel and Bio Pharma undertakings transfer to dedicated resulting companies; IGL Spirits will hold potable spirits, Bio-Fuel and biopolymers; Ennature retains nutraceuticals and APIs. Effective date not yet communicated.
demand_pricing: Spirits: management says the industry grew at a 4-5% CAGR over the last one to two years; IMFL growth attributed to launches in deluxe whisky, semi-premium vodka and white spirits. Prestige & Above volume ~0.5 million cases, roughly double last year.
Mix: revenue lagged volume in Spirits because of state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium grew faster).

Chemicals: ethylene oxide became similar to or slightly cheaper than Reliance's EO for a few months, increasing specialty chemicals off-take. Oil and gas and Middle East exports were hit by propylene oxide shortages and freight volatility (westbound freight up 5-20x).
Ennature: raw material availability and pricing volatile and a challenge in Q2 as well.

qa_highlights.question: What is the guidance for potable spirits for FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 EBITDA above INR500 crore, with INR120 crore delivered in Q1; volume to double versus last year, with healthy double-digit growth expected next year.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for the NSU (chemicals) business and how will it scale?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex limited to about INR5-20 crore this year; cumulative new plant investment about INR50-60 crore. Aspiration of INR150 crore-plus revenue this year and INR600-700 crore in 4-5 years, with margins improving over time.

qa_highlights.question: Are JV profits sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a fair assumption; JV PAT about INR19 crore a year ago versus INR21 crore now, with the improvement linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage.

qa_highlights.question: Prestige & Above volumes and IMFL revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A about 0.5 million cases, roughly double last year. FY26 IMFL volume was 3.4 million cases; FY26 IMFL revenue was not disclosed and will be sent later.

qa_highlights.question: Why did volumes grow faster than revenue in Spirits?
qa_highlights.answer: Attributed to state mix (Delhi growth lower margin) and brand mix (mass premium growing faster); revenue growth expected to exceed volume growth as premium mix rises.

qa_highlights.question: What is the IMFL margin versus country liquor?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margins in deluxe and semi-premium whisky are almost the same as in P&A and did not give separate EBITDA margins.

risks_watch: Demerger effectiveness date not yet communicated; NCLT sanctioned the scheme on 17 July 2026 and the three-entity reporting structure depends on effectiveness.

Sustainability of JV profit: JV PAT about INR21 crore this quarter versus about INR19 crore a year ago, linked to narrower EO cost disadvantage versus Reliance; management called it a fair assumption.
Ennature raw material availability and pricing volatile; described as a challenge in Q2 as well.
Chemicals performance chemicals growth of 40% was below target; oil and gas and Middle East exports hit by propylene oxide shortages and westbound freight volatility (5-20x).
Quarter-on-quarter EBITDA comparison distorted by Q4 FY26 Clariant dividend income of about INR39 crore; a shareholder query on quarterly EBITDA trend was deferred to email.
Spirits FY27 guidance (EBITDA above INR500 crore, IMFL volume roughly double) and FY26 IMFL revenue not yet disclosed; FY26 IMFL revenue to be sent later.

summary.management_tone: Management was confident and upbeat on Spirits and Ennature, but repeatedly qualified forward-looking figures as aspirations rather than guidance, for example the chemicals INR400 crore EBITDA target and the Ennature INR130-150 crore EBITDA target. It was more cautious on performance chemicals, which grew below target, and deferred several detailed questions (FY26 IMFL revenue, royalty to Amrut, quarterly EBITDA trend) to follow-up.
